e8_lattice.flavour: Two hundred and forty roots, each touching the same number of neighbours, packed so tightly in eight dimensions that no sphere could be added anywhere. Viazovska proved it optimal in 2016. Held up to the light, the crystal seems to show a different symmetric face no matter how I turn it, as though it has more sides than my hand can count.
e8_lattice.discovery: Octonions and the Hopf fibration kept pointing at the same structure, so I fed both into the Tesseract Assembler with a G2 manifold and a little exotic matter. The lattice that came out was the one every symmetry I had studied was secretly a shadow of.

cantor_key.flavour: A key whose teeth are a diagonal: each one differs from the matching tooth of every other key that could ever be cut. It fits no lock in the ordinary world, and turning it feels like stepping off the end of the number line and finding the floor continues anyway.
cantor_key.discovery: Cantor's diagonal argument shows that no list can contain every real number. I built the argument into hardware - a natural number lattice, an aleph-null shard and a power set - and mounted it on a brane shifter. The key opened onto the place where the bigger infinities live.

false_vacuum_membrane.flavour: A thin, shivering film that seems to hold two different kinds of emptiness apart. One side is our vacuum, the other a lower-energy one that would rather replace it. It is cold and faintly elastic, and I handle it the way one handles a soap bubble that could end the universe if it popped wrong.
false_vacuum_membrane.discovery: The Vacuum Drifters glide without quite touching our space. When I finally brought one down, its body collapsed and left only this skin behind - the domain wall it had been carrying around between its own vacuum and ours.

hotel_key.flavour: A brass key with a tag that always reads one number higher than the last time I looked. Hilbert's Hotel has infinitely many rooms, all full, and still has space for a new guest: everyone just moves up by one. The key is warm, as if someone has only now handed it over.
hotel_key.discovery: I found it in a drawer of the infinite hotel, and later prised more from the hands of the Bellhops who shuffle guests from room n to room n+1. The tag changed while I was reading it, which was my first proof that the hotel was taking its own rule seriously.

brane_tether.flavour: A cord that binds my mass to our three-dimensional membrane. In brane-world models ordinary matter is stuck to the brane while gravity alone leaks into the bulk; the tether makes sure I stay stuck too. It hums against the wrist like a plucked string, tugging gently toward somewhere I cannot point to.
brane_tether.discovery: My first trip into the Bulk nearly smeared me across a dimension I have no organs for. I wound a graviton crystal and a metric tensor around a neutronium spine, timed with a chronon capacitor, so that the metric always pulls me back onto our brane.

primordial_charter.flavour: A sheet of crystal on which the laws of physics are written as they were before any symmetry broke - one force, no masses, nothing yet decided. Reading it is like looking at the draft of a constitution that every later amendment has forgotten. Its edges are perfectly sharp.
primordial_charter.discovery: Hyperdimensional Reality kept rewriting me to fit its own laws. I wove axiom fragments and a source code fragment through a transfinite weave and pinned it with a reality anchor, hoping a copy of the original laws would remind the place who I was. It did.

form_of_the_self.flavour: A small crystal figure, faceted and without flaw, that is unmistakably me - not as I am but as Plato would have said I am meant to be. In the Realm of Forms every imperfect copy defers to its ideal, and this is the ideal I can point to when the Realm asks who I claim to be.
form_of_the_self.discovery: The Platonic Realm treated me as a poor copy of something and tried to correct me. I cut Cherenkov quartz around a quantum dot that held my own readings, and set it in a Cherenkov lattice. With an ideal to answer to, the Realm stopped trying to fix me.

coherence_stabiliser.flavour: A humming lattice that keeps my wavefunction from decohering into a thousand slightly different versions of me. Normally the environment measures a body constantly; this device shelters me from enough of that scrutiny to stay one thing. It feels heavier when I think about it too hard.
coherence_stabiliser.discovery: In the Quantum Foam I watched my own outline blur into overlapping drafts. I braided an entangled photon pair through a quantum field lattice and a spin foam lattice on a chronosteel frame, so that it carries the decoherence away from me instead.

well_ordering_charm.flavour: A pendant of nested rings, each smaller than the one before, with no ring missing and none endless. It embodies the well-ordering principle: every non-empty set of ordinals has a least element, so every descending chain must stop. In a place full of infinities, it is comforting to wear a guarantee of a bottom.
well_ordering_charm.discovery: The Transfinite Hierarchy kept dropping me into staircases that went down forever. I set a surreal number inside rings cut from a power set and an aleph-null shard, and the charm forced every descent to end. I have not fallen forever since.

identity_kernel.flavour: A tiny, dense seed that holds the minimal description of me - not the body, not the memories, but whatever remains invariant when everything else is stripped away. It is almost weightless and yet the hand closes around it reflexively, as if it knew what it was holding.
identity_kernel.discovery: The Transcendental dissolves anything that cannot say what it is. I compressed my own pattern through an ontological processor and a cognitive singularity, and anchored it to the omega point on a transfinite weave. What survived the compression was the kernel.

graviton_harness.flavour: A web of straps and plates that takes the pull of a crushing field and spreads it through every bone at once, so no single joint bears it. Tidal forces kill by difference, not by strength; the harness erases the difference. Wearing it feels like being hugged by a planet.
graviton_harness.discovery: A walk through a high-gravity field nearly broke both my ankles. I laid graviton crystals across neutronium plating and added an inertia damper to smooth the gradients, so that the field pulls on all of me equally and none of me in particular.

chronal_anchor.flavour: A heavy pendulum sealed in chronosteel that keeps my own clock ticking at its proper rate while the world outside speeds up or slows down. Proper time is personal in relativity; this makes sure mine stays mine. Its ticking is the calmest sound I have ever heard.
chronal_anchor.discovery: Inside a dilated time field my heartbeat and my thoughts drifted out of step. I tied a temporal knot to an arrow of time shard and fed it from a chronon capacitor, so my clock is referenced against itself rather than against the field.

proof_of_everything.flavour: A single page, endlessly dense, that ends with a square marking the proof complete. I cannot follow every line, but each line I do read follows from the last. It is not a theory of everything so much as evidence that I was capable of understanding one. It is very quiet to hold.
proof_of_everything.discovery: Alpha Omega did not die so much as concede. When its last trial was answered it left this behind - a proof, signed in my own reasoning, that the work was done. Only with it in hand did the door to the Transcendental admit me.

entanglement_tuner.flavour: A slim instrument with a dial that sets which entangled channel a transceiver listens on. Entanglement cannot carry a message by itself, but it can share a key and a correlation; the tuner makes two devices agree on which pair of photons they share. It clicks softly between settings.
entanglement_tuner.discovery: My transceivers kept pairing with whichever partner was nearest. I mounted an entangled photon pair and a quantum dot on a neutronium plate as a reference, so every device I tune shares the same correlated source and stays on one channel.

empirical_dossier.flavour: A thick binder of my earliest discoveries - every measurement, every failed run, every note in the margin - bound and sealed in superfluid-cooled pages. Read by a machine, it is a curriculum. Read by me, it is mostly embarrassment and nostalgia in roughly equal parts.
empirical_dossier.discovery: Teaching a machine to study meant giving it something to study. I gathered the three volumes of my empirical notes and preserved them in superfluid helium, so the Research Nexus could read them as I once did - only faster. I have found copies in anomaly vaults too.

theoretical_dossier.flavour: The middle chapters of my research: dense theory, half of it proven, half of it argued with myself in the margins. It is bound over the earlier empirical dossier, the way theory sits on observation. Exotic matter keeps the binding from aging, which is just as well.
theoretical_dossier.discovery: Once a mind could improve itself, it could also read what I had built and extend it. I compiled the three theoretical volumes over the empirical dossier and fixed them with exotic matter, and the Research Nexus started asking questions I had not.

unified_dossier.flavour: Everything I know up to the brink of pure mathematics, pressed into one volume until the separate fields are no longer separable. The pages are slightly damp with synaptic fluid, as if the book had been thinking. Opening it anywhere lands on something connected to everything else.
unified_dossier.discovery: Learning to compress a whole field into one point taught me to compress my notes the same way. I stacked the three unified volumes on the theoretical dossier, soaked them in synaptic fluid, and the result read less like a book and more like a single idea.

absolute_dossier.flavour: The research record of a civilisation that has very nearly finished understanding its universe. Its cover is primordial law itself, so the book reads like a document from before the universe decided its rules. It weighs exactly what I expect it to, which unsettles me more than anything.
absolute_dossier.discovery: To build the Omnilex Engine I needed a machine that knew everything I did. I bound the three absolute volumes over the unified dossier with primordial law, and for the first time the Research Nexus had nothing left to ask me.

empirical_notes_1.flavour: A sheaf of first-hand observations from the hardest experiments of my early work: time's arrow, a kugelblitz forming, gravitons, a stellar core, a monopole. The handwriting gets worse as the experiments get stranger. Every page smells faintly of ozone.
empirical_notes_1.discovery: When I first tried to teach a machine to study, I realised my raw notes were scattered across every lab. Pressing an arrow of time shard, a kugelblitz seed, a magnetic monopole and their kin into the Femtoscale line made them into a record a machine could read.

empirical_notes_2.flavour: The second third of my empirical record: psionic crystals, attosecond capacitors, strange and charm quarks, quaternions and the complex plane, tachyon klystrons. It is the most chaotic volume, the one where physics and mathematics start to bleed into each other on the page.
empirical_notes_2.discovery: Assembling the second volume showed me how much of my early work was really mathematics in disguise. A quaternion crystal and the complex plane sat beside quarks and a tachyon klystron, and the Femtoscale line wove them into one coherent set of notes.

empirical_notes_3.flavour: The final third of the early record: gravitational lensing, all six quark flavours, spacetime lattices, fractals, neurons built of light. It ends abruptly, mid-thought, where I stopped measuring and started theorising. The last page is mostly arrows.
empirical_notes_3.discovery: Bottom and top quarks next to up and down, a Minkowski lattice beside a fractal set, a gravitic lens element and a photonic neuron - closing the empirical record meant gathering the pieces that bridged particles, geometry and minds.

theoretical_notes_1.flavour: The opening volume of my theoretical period, written as I began to think in megastructures: Dyson shells, self-replicating probes, calibrators that adjust themselves, topos theory. The ideas are big enough that the notebook seems too small for them.
theoretical_notes_1.discovery: Once I could build a self-improving mind, I needed it to read my theory. I fed an autonomous calibrator, a Dyson shell segment, a topos, a von Neumann probe and r-process nuclei into the Femtoscale line to set down the first theoretical volume.

theoretical_notes_2.flavour: The middle volume of my theory: superintelligent cores, M-branes, compactified dimensions curled small, armour plates of degenerate matter, the slag left when spacetime is overworked. It reads like a manual for an engineer working on the universe from the outside.
theoretical_notes_2.discovery: Putting the second theoretical volume together meant compressing string theory and stellar engineering onto the same pages - an M-brane and a compactified circle bound with degenerate armour plate, spacetime slag and cosmic neutronium.

theoretical_notes_3.flavour: The last theoretical volume: category theory, the multiverse, string coupling, metallic hydrogen, supernovae and gravitational waves. By the final page I was drawing commutative diagrams in the margins of an astrophysics paper and not noticing.
theoretical_notes_3.discovery: I closed the theoretical record with the pieces that tied structure to cosmos: a category lattice, a multiverse shard and a string coupling crystal beside a supernova remnant and a gravitational wave crystal. The Femtoscale line made them read as one argument.

unified_notes_1.flavour: The first unified volume, where infinity, hypernova metallurgy, reality anchors, geodesics and quantum superposition sit in the same paragraph without apology. Nothing here belongs to a single discipline any more. The paper itself seems to bend slightly along the lines of text.
unified_notes_1.discovery: Compressing a field into a point taught me to compress my notes too. Absolute infinity, a hypernova alloy ingot, a reality anchor, a geodesic thread, a superposition crystal and an eigenstate lattice went in; one volume of unified theory came out.

unified_notes_2.flavour: The middle unified volume: countable infinity, catalysts of eternity, the Christoffel symbols of curved space, pocket universes, white holes, gravitons. Every page cross-references three others. It is a delight to read and almost impossible to summarise.
unified_notes_2.discovery: I bound an aleph-null shard to a Christoffel symbol and a pocket universe to a white hole fragment, with an eternity catalyst and a graviton crystal to hold the threads. The Femtoscale line found the common thread I had been sensing for months.

unified_notes_3.flavour: The last unified volume: surreal numbers, the omega point, degenerate matter, the stress-energy tensor, causal loops with no origin, magnetic monopoles. It is where my notes stop distinguishing between what is true of matter and what is true of number.
unified_notes_3.discovery: To close the unified record I needed the strangest proofs I owned: a surreal number, the omega point, a bootstrap artifact that has no beginning, a stress-energy tensor, degenerate matter and a monopole. Woven together, they read as a single theory.

absolute_notes_1.flavour: The first of the final volumes: axioms, paradoxes, the Banach-Tarski sphere that doubles itself, and Godel's sentence that says it cannot be proven. It is a notebook about the foundations of thought, written by someone standing on them while they shake.
absolute_notes_1.discovery: The Omnilex required notes about the rules beneath the rules. I fed an axiom fragment, paradox residue, an axiomatic field emitter, a white hole fragment, a Banach-Tarski sphere and a Godel sentence into the line, and the first absolute volume came out signed.

absolute_notes_2.flavour: The middle absolute volume: crystallised law, a theory of everything, neutronium, the first uncountable cardinal, the E8 lattice and the Hopf fibration. It is where the most elegant structures I have found are set side by side, and it is beautiful in a way that makes me slightly afraid.
absolute_notes_2.discovery: I gathered the most symmetric things I had made - an E8 lattice, a Hopf fibration, aleph-one, a theory of everything and crystallised law - and bound them with neutronium. The Femtoscale line produced the volume that I now consider my best work.

absolute_notes_3.flavour: The last volume of all: the axiom key, absolute infinity, pocket universes, axiom schemas, epsilon-naught and an inaccessible cardinal. It ends where mathematics itself ends. I read it once, closed it, and went for a long walk.
absolute_notes_3.discovery: For the closing volume I needed the largest objects I had ever handled - an inaccessible cardinal, epsilon-naught, absolute infinity - with an axiom key and an axiom schema to frame them. Pressed together with a pocket universe, they finished the record.

zeolite_catalyst.flavour: An aluminosilicate crystal riddled with channels the width of a single molecule. Anything that fits inside is held in exactly the right pose to react, so reactions that would idle in open air happen in a blink. It is light, chalky and faintly gritty, like pumice that remembers being a mineral.
zeolite_catalyst.discovery: Clay and quartz dissolved in supercritical solvent recrystallised into a sponge of perfect pores. With a pinch of Cherenkov quartz as a template the channels came out uniform, and molecules small enough to enter came out changed.

molecular_orbital_lattice.flavour: Electron clouds shared across a whole grid of atoms, frozen in place so I can finally see what a bond is: not a stick between balls but a wavefunction spread over both, lower in energy than either alone. The lattice shimmers faintly where the orbitals overlap.
molecular_orbital_lattice.discovery: Solving the Schrodinger equation for a molecule taught me where the electrons sit. I used a qubit to encode that solution and grew the crystal around it on a zeolite template in supercritical solvent, so the orbitals set exactly where the mathematics put them.

chiral_crystal.flavour: A crystal that comes in only one hand. Like my left and right palms, its mirror image cannot be rotated to match it. Living things use left-handed amino acids and right-handed sugars, and nobody fully knows why. This one twists light passing through it, always the same way.
chiral_crystal.discovery: Molecular orbitals let me predict which hand a molecule would take. Seeding an orbital lattice with amethyst and a quantum dot in supercritical solvent, I found the crystals all came out with the same handedness. I stopped calling it an accident after the tenth batch.

electride_crystal.flavour: A salt in which the negative ions are not atoms at all but bare electrons, sitting in cavities of the lattice like eggs in a carton. It is dark, glossy and conducts strangely, and seems to give up electrons at the slightest provocation.
electride_crystal.discovery: Pushing electrons into Cherenkov quartz with redstone current, while superfluid helium held the lattice cold and still, I found that some electrons stayed behind in empty sites with no atom to belong to. The Electrolytic Cell had made an electride.

graphene_sheet.flavour: A single layer of carbon atoms in a honeycomb, so thin it is almost invisible yet stronger than steel by weight and a better conductor than copper. Folded in the hand it feels like nothing, and then it does not tear.
graphene_sheet.discovery: Peeling graphite with tape works, but slowly. I let nanites strip coal down to single layers on a zeolite catalyst in supercritical solvent, and the Chemical Reactor gave me whole sheets in one run.

carbon_nanotube_bundle.flavour: Graphene sheets rolled seamlessly into tubes a few nanometres across, then twisted together into a rope. Each tube is far stronger than steel; the bundle feels like silk and refuses to snap. Pulled taut, it sings faintly.
carbon_nanotube_bundle.discovery: Graphene curled on its own along the edges of an orbital lattice, so I gave it more lattice and an ionic liquid to roll in. The tubes came out closed and clean, and twisted into rope as they dried.

buckyball_cage.flavour: Sixty carbon atoms bonded into the shape of a football - twelve pentagons and twenty hexagons - with a hollow centre big enough to trap one more atom. It is round, slippery and perfectly symmetrical, and the hollow seems to be waiting for something.
buckyball_cage.discovery: Heating graphene with blaze powder, I expected soot. Instead the sheets curled into closed spheres, and cooled in superfluid helium they stayed that way - the same cages Kroto and Smalley found in vaporised graphite.

metal_organic_framework.flavour: A scaffold of copper nodes and organic struts so open that a single gram of it hides more inner surface than a football pitch. Gas soaks into it like water into a sponge. It is feather-light and full of rooms.
metal_organic_framework.discovery: Supramolecular chemistry lets molecules assemble themselves. Copper ions met nanotube struts and chiral linkers in an ionic liquid, and each found its place without my help. The framework grew the way frost grows on glass.

noble_gas_clathrate.flavour: A cage of ice with a xenon atom trapped in every cell, held not by bonds but by the plain fact that it cannot get out. The noble gases are supposed to be aloof; caged like this they are merely patient. It fizzes slightly as it warms.
noble_gas_clathrate.discovery: Ice frozen around buckyball templates in superfluid helium formed cages of a very particular size. Noble gas filled them before I could seal the reactor, and stayed. Clathrates were not a goal - they were a pleasant accident.

self_healing_polymer.flavour: A rubbery strip that, cut cleanly in two, slowly finds itself again. Its chains carry reversible bonds that break and reform, so pressing the halves together lets them rebond across the seam. It is warm and a little sticky at the cut.
self_healing_polymer.discovery: I wanted a material that repaired itself the way skin does. Nanotube rope gave it strength, slime gave it reversible bonds, and a topological circuit board gave the bonds a pattern to restore. The first sample healed overnight.

room_temperature_superconductor.flavour: A dark wafer through which current flows with zero resistance at ordinary temperatures. Electrons pair up into Cooper pairs and move through the lattice as one coherent wave. A magnet hovers over it, locked in place. Physicists have chased this for a century.
room_temperature_superconductor.discovery: Hydrogen-rich compounds superconduct at high temperature, but only under crushing pressure. I let metallic hydrogen fill a metal-organic framework, doped it with an electride and seeded it with a condensate, so the cage held the pressure for me.

positronium_hydride.flavour: A molecule built from a hydrogen atom and positronium - an electron orbiting its own antiparticle. Left free it annihilates in about a nanosecond in a flash of gamma rays. Trapped in a carbon cage it lingers, faintly warm, as if counting down.
positronium_hydride.discovery: Positronium forms whenever positrons slow down in matter, and it pairs with hydrogen briefly before it dies. I gave it a buckyball cage to hide in and a carborane superacid to supply protons, and the molecule held.

muonic_catalyst.flavour: A capsule of molecules in which electrons are replaced by muons, two hundred times heavier. The orbitals shrink accordingly, and two nuclei that would never fuse at room temperature are pulled close enough to tunnel into one. It feels oddly heavy for its size.
muonic_catalyst.discovery: Muon-catalysed fusion was known in the 1950s; its problem is that muons are short-lived and get stuck. Using a noble gas clathrate to hold the fuel, quark-gluon plasma to make muons and a monopole to free them, I got the catalyst to work cycle after cycle.

flerovium_ingot.flavour: Element 114, a superheavy metal held together by a near-magic number of protons. Real flerovium lasts seconds; this ingot lasts indefinitely because its neutron count sits right on the island. It is improbably dense and faintly warm.
flerovium_ingot.discovery: The island of stability predicts superheavy nuclei that live long. I fed r-process clusters and neutronium into the Nuclide Forge with muons to tighten the nuclei and quark-gluon plasma to supply neutrons, and something came out that did not immediately decay.

unbihexium_ingot.flavour: Element 126, the heart of the island of stability, where magic numbers for both protons and neutrons line up. Nothing this heavy should last; this does. Its surface is a dull silver that seems to swallow light.
unbihexium_ingot.discovery: Flerovium on its own is only the shore of the island. Pushing further meant adding supernova debris, positronium hydride to supply energy and quark-gluon plasma for neutrons. The Nuclide Forge produced element 126 and it stayed.

gene_sampler.flavour: A slim needle on a neutronium handle, tipped with a quantum dot that reads base pairs as it draws them. One quick touch takes a genome sample. Touch a creature from another dimension and the dot reads something that is not DNA at all.
gene_sampler.discovery: I needed a way to copy a creature's blueprint without harming it. A quantum dot on a stick, backed by neutronium so it would not flex, was enough to read a genome on contact. The first creature I sampled barely noticed.

genome_sample.flavour: A vial of clear fluid with every instruction for building one creature written in four chemical letters. It looks like water. It is the most information-dense thing I have ever casually put in my pocket.
genome_sample.discovery: The Gene Sampler's first touch filled a vial with a creature's complete genome. Sequencing it showed the same alphabet as my own, which was both expected and moving.

xenogenome_sample.flavour: A vial of something that is clearly a genome but is not DNA. The molecule folds the wrong way, uses letters I do not recognise and carries information more densely than any terrestrial code. It glows faintly in the dark.
xenogenome_sample.discovery: I sampled a creature from another dimension expecting DNA and found something else. Life evolved under different physics, with a different chemistry of inheritance - and it was still readable.

recombinant_dna.flavour: A double helix spliced together from more than one creature, its pieces joined by enzymes that cut and paste at precise sequences. It looks no different from any other DNA. It does things no single creature's DNA could.
recombinant_dna.discovery: Restriction enzymes cut genomes at precise points; ligases stitch them back. I let engineered enzymes splice two samples together in a nutrient broth, and the Gene Sequencer read back a genome that had never existed before.

engineered_enzyme.flavour: A protein designed rather than evolved, folded around a pocket shaped for exactly one reaction. It speeds that reaction a millionfold and ignores everything else. It looks like a pale, slightly sticky crystal.
engineered_enzyme.discovery: Natural enzymes are evolved to fit their substrates. I started from a genome, used a chiral crystal to fix the handedness and a zeolite to shape the pocket, then let the Bioreactor optimise the rest in nutrient broth.

folded_protein_crystal.flavour: A long chain of amino acids that has found its one native shape out of more possible shapes than there are atoms in the universe - and frozen in that shape as a crystal. Levinthal's paradox says it should take forever. It took milliseconds.
folded_protein_crystal.discovery: Proteins fold quickly because the energy landscape funnels them. I mapped that funnel with a molecular orbital lattice, let a quantum processor search it, and grew the folded chain from recombinant DNA in nutrient broth.

stem_cell_culture.flavour: A flask of cells that have not yet decided what to become. Any of them could be a neuron, a muscle, a bone. The broth is warm and cloudy and seems to be thinking about its options. Under the microscope they look identical, and that sameness is exactly the point: every possibility is still open.
stem_cell_culture.discovery: Synthetic biology lets me write life rather than read it. I took a genome sample, spliced in recombinant DNA to undo specialisation and used an engineered enzyme to hold the cells in their undecided state.

synthetic_cell.flavour: The smallest genome that can still be alive, written base by base and booted inside a membrane. It does almost nothing but live, eat and divide. Watching it divide for the first time felt like watching a program run.
synthetic_cell.discovery: Venter's team built a minimal cell by stripping a bacterium's genome down. I wrote mine from recombinant DNA, wrapped it in self-healing polymer, fed it nutrient broth and used a buckyball as a cofactor. It divided.

xenobot_swarm.flavour: Living machines a millimetre across, built from cells arranged in shapes no animal ever had. They walk, push, heal and even assemble copies of themselves from loose cells. They twitch in the jar, busy.
xenobot_swarm.discovery: Xenobots were real: frog cells arranged by an evolutionary algorithm. I gave a general AI core stem cells and nanites to design with, and the Bioreactor built whatever shape it picked. Some of them built more of themselves.

tardigrade_culture.flavour: A culture of water bears, tiny eight-legged animals that survive vacuum, radiation and freezing by drying out and simply pausing being alive. In the jar they wander slowly through moss. Dried, they will wait for centuries.
tardigrade_culture.discovery: Extremophiles taught me that life could survive almost anything. I used engineered enzymes to boost a tardigrade genome's repair genes, gave them moss to live in and froze a culture in superfluid helium. It woke up.

quantum_chlorophyll.flavour: Chlorophyll molecules arranged so precisely that the energy of absorbed light explores every pathway to the reaction centre at once, coherently, and takes the best one. Real photosynthesis does this. This sample does it perfectly, and glows a deep, almost violet green.
quantum_chlorophyll.discovery: Quantum biology shows that photosynthesis uses coherence to route energy. I folded the light-harvesting proteins precisely, entangled their pathways with a photon pair and grew them in kelp and nutrient broth. The efficiency was nearly total.

cryptochrome_magnetoreceptor.flavour: A protein from a robin's eye that senses Earth's magnetic field through a pair of entangled electron spins. Light makes the pair; the field tips their dance. The crystal turns slowly in the hand to point north.
cryptochrome_magnetoreceptor.discovery: Migratory birds see magnetic fields, probably via radical pairs in cryptochrome. I folded the protein from feather genetics, entangled its radical pair with a photon pair and grew it in nutrient broth. It aligned with the field.

neural_organoid.flavour: A pea-sized brain grown in a dish: real neurons, folded and connected, with no body around them. Its electrical activity has started to look like the patterns of a sleeping brain. I try not to think about what it might be dreaming about.
neural_organoid.discovery: Brain organoids are a real technology. I grew stem cells around a thought matrix with a room-temperature superconductor for wiring and fed them synaptic fluid. Within days the electrodes recorded coordinated waves.

turing_morphogen.flavour: A pair of chemicals, one that activates and diffuses slowly and one that inhibits and diffuses fast. Mixed on a dish they paint stripes and spots by themselves, exactly the reaction-diffusion patterns Turing predicted in 1952.
turing_morphogen.discovery: Turing proposed that patterns in animals arise from reaction and diffusion. I extracted the morphogens from a minimal cell, set their handedness with a chiral crystal and tuned their rates using the complex plane. Spots appeared on the dish.

silicon_life_spore.flavour: A spore built on silicon instead of carbon - a speculative chemistry that only works in the strange physics of the Bulk. It is glassy, faceted and very slightly warm, and it ticks quietly, as though growing at the pace of crystal.
silicon_life_spore.discovery: Silicon life has always been a thought experiment. In the Bulk, where chemistry runs differently, I seeded a minimal cell with a xenogenome and Xenoplasm on a bulk crystal. The spore that grew was neither carbon nor stone.

telomerase_complex.flavour: An enzyme that rebuilds telomeres - the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes that shorten every time a cell divides. Cells that have it do not age. The complex is small, pale and oddly cold, as if keeping time for itself.
telomerase_complex.discovery: Telomerase is real; most adult cells have switched it off. The Evolution Engine ran a million generations of stem cells and tardigrades with Turing morphogens and Xenoplasm, while an arrow of time shard kept the clock running fast.

spark_of_life.flavour: A small bright point that is the moment chemistry crossed into biology - self-replication, metabolism and a boundary, all arriving at once. It flickers unsteadily. Holding it feels like holding a match that might become a forest.
spark_of_life.discovery: Abiogenesis is the unsolved step. I put primordial soup, stellar plasma and the omega point in the Abiogenesis Crucible with telomerase, a minimal cell and quantum chlorophyll, and caught the instant it all started to copy itself.

panspermia_seed.flavour: A seed packed with life designed to survive the trip between universes. Tardigrade toughness, a spark of life and unbihexium shielding, all sealed in a capsule that seems to hold a small universe of its own. It is light and very still.
panspermia_seed.discovery: Panspermia supposes life travels between worlds. I wanted it to travel between universes. The Abiogenesis Crucible sealed a spark of life with tardigrades, Xenoplasm and primordial soup inside a bubble universe shielded by unbihexium.

omnicellular_genome.flavour: One genome that can build any creature in any dimension - carbon or silicon, DNA or not. It is a coiled, shifting helix that seems to change alphabet as I watch. Every living thing I have met is a sentence it can write.
omnicellular_genome.discovery: I fed the Evolution Engine a panspermia seed, a silicon life spore, a neural organoid, recombinant DNA and Xenoplasm and let it evolve a single code that could express all of them. It took less time than I feared.

containment_cell.flavour: An empty flask of containment-field glass with an iron frame, its walls held by a magnetic seal rather than by chemistry. It will hold plasma, superfluids or things stranger than either. Empty, it hums faintly, waiting.
containment_cell.discovery: Buckets melt, crack or leak. I built a flask from iron and containment field glass so that a magnetic seal, not the walls, holds the contents. I have found a few already-made cells in anomaly vaults as well.

assembly_matrix.flavour: A femtoscale jig that holds a hundred tiny parts exactly in place while the Extreme Assembly Table joins them. It is small, heavy and covered in fine engraved channels, and it seems to settle into the hand like a tool that knows its job.
assembly_matrix.discovery: Assembling parts smaller than a proton by hand is impossible. I combined photonic and quantum processors with a metamaterial frame and chronosteel so that the matrix positions every part itself while the table does the joining.

hyperlattice_frame.flavour: A scaffold folded through a fourth dimension so that a nine-by-nine assembly has room for everything inside it. From any angle it looks slightly too small to hold what it holds. Its corners never quite meet where the eye expects.
hyperlattice_frame.discovery: The Extreme Assembly Table kept running out of space. A tesseract core gave the frame a fourth dimension to fold into, and graviton crystals held the fold steady. The frame is bigger on the inside, in the honest geometric sense.

transfinite_weave.flavour: A cloth woven with more threads than there are natural numbers to count them - an uncountable weave in the honest Cantorian sense. It drapes like silk, and every thread is visible no matter how close I look. The endgame assemblies are stitched on it.
transfinite_weave.discovery: Cantor showed some infinities are larger than others. I used an aleph-null shard as the warp and let a cosmic processor diagonalise across it to produce the weft. The result was a cloth that cannot be listed.

oracle_lemma.flavour: A slip of paper bearing a lemma that settles whatever it is shown. Its proof is not written anywhere - it is simply assumed, as an oracle's answers are. Holding it feels a little like cheating, which is because it is.
oracle_lemma.discovery: This came from outside my research entirely: an oracle that answers a trial without the work. Used in one of Alpha Omega's chambers, it counts as solved. I keep it for testing and try not to think about what it implies.

deepslate_cherenkov_quartz_ore.flavour: Dark deepslate shot through with pale blue veins that glow faintly, the way water glows around a reactor core when particles outrun light in that medium. Deep under the surface the quartz has been soaking up cosmic-ray muons for a very long time.
deepslate_cherenkov_quartz_ore.discovery: I first noticed it as a faint blue gleam on a deepslate wall far below the surface, too dim to be lava and the wrong colour for anything I knew. The pick confirmed it was the same quartz as nearer the surface, only deeper.

degenerate_matter_ore.flavour: End stone cracked around knots of matter so compressed that its electrons are packed into the lowest states quantum mechanics permits. Pauli exclusion holds it up, not chemistry. The block is far heavier than it looks, and the pick rings against it.
degenerate_matter_ore.discovery: In the End, where dead stars seem to have been scattered, a pickaxe bounced off a seam of end stone that was much too heavy. Under the crust was matter pressed into degeneracy, like a fragment of a white dwarf.

void_lattice_ore.flavour: Bulk stone holding pockets of a crystal made of nothing - a lattice of empty sites that remains rigid even though there is nothing in them. It looks like a gap in the rock that has decided to be solid.
void_lattice_ore.discovery: Mining in the Bulk, I hit a patch of rock that the pick went through as though it were air but that still dropped something. The lattice was a crystal of vacancies, ordered without anything to order.

bulk_stone.flavour: The bedrock of the higher-dimensional Bulk: a grey stone that seems to have more surfaces than it shows. Edges blur where the extra dimensions curl back in. It is cool and unremarkable to the touch, which is somehow worse.
bulk_stone.discovery: Everything in the Bulk rests on this stone, and I first broke some off to see if the extra dimensions would follow it home. They did, a little - enough to make it useful in crafting.

bulk_crystal.flavour: A translucent crystal from the Bulk whose facets seem to point in directions I cannot quite name. Light passing through comes out a little out of phase with itself, as if it had taken a short detour through another axis.
bulk_crystal.discovery: I found these growing in the Bulk where the extra dimensions are most tightly curled. Looking through one, I saw my own hand from an angle I should not have been able to see it from.

neutronium_block.flavour: A cube of compacted neutronium, matter in which electrons and protons have been crushed together into neutrons. It is almost impossibly dense for its size, and dropping it on a floor would be a mistake. The surface is a smooth, dull grey.
neutronium_block.discovery: Storing loose neutronium ingots wasted space, so I pressed nine together. The block holds its shape with nothing but the strong force, and it makes a convenient compact supply.

cherenkov_quartz_block.flavour: Nine pieces of Cherenkov quartz fused into a single block that glows the soft blue of particles outrunning light in a medium. It is cool, translucent and slightly brighter in the dark than any ordinary stone should be.
cherenkov_quartz_block.discovery: Compacting Cherenkov quartz made storage easier and, as a bonus, the larger crystal glowed more strongly. I started building with it before I had a reason to.

spacetime_casing.flavour: A casing whose plating is neutronium, whose seams are Cherenkov quartz and whose interior is folded slightly with ender pearls so it holds a little more than it should. It is the standard skin for any machine that bends the rules near it.
spacetime_casing.discovery: Every machine I built that warped spacetime warped its own housing too. Neutronium resisted, Cherenkov quartz shed the excess energy as light, and an ender pearl's fold gave the inside room to breathe.

event_horizon_casing.flavour: A casing with a dark metamaterial skin over spacetime casing and neutronium plate: whatever reaches it from inside does not come back out. It is utterly black and seems to absorb the edges of nearby objects.
event_horizon_casing.discovery: Machines handling black holes needed housings that behaved like horizons. A metamaterial sheet that bends light around itself, over neutronium plate and spacetime casing, made a one-way wall.

hyperframe_casing.flavour: A casing laced with topological insulator and superposition crystal, so that its interior exists in several overlapping configurations at once. It looks solid but sounds slightly hollow, as though echoing in a direction I cannot see.
hyperframe_casing.discovery: Hyperdimensional machines needed a frame that could be in more than one shape. Topological insulators conduct only on the surface and superposition crystals hold several states, and together over spacetime casing they gave the frame its depth.

containment_field_glass.flavour: Glass that is not really glass, but a field held between two panes with a shimmer of plasma in between. It holds back heat, cold and pressure that would shatter any ordinary window, and it hums faintly when touched.
containment_field_glass.discovery: I needed windows that could watch a reaction without melting. I gave up on the glass and trusted the field instead, which holds the reaction and lets the light pass through.

superconducting_coil_block.flavour: A drum of superconducting coil wound around spacetime casing. Current, once started, circulates in it forever with no loss at all. The field it makes tugs gently at anything metal nearby. Frost gathers along the windings, a reminder of how cold the wire must stay.
superconducting_coil_block.discovery: Large machines needed strong, steady fields. Winding superconducting coil around spacetime casing gave me a coil that carries current indefinitely without heating, and a magnetic field that never flags.

field_emitter.flavour: A compact emitter of neutronium plate, Cherenkov quartz and a quantum dot that projects a field shaped by the dot's quantum state. Change the state, change the field. It sits warm and quiet, faintly buzzing.
field_emitter.discovery: Multiblocks kept needing local fields of different shapes. A quantum dot can hold a programmed state, and Cherenkov quartz can turn that state into a field. I have also found ready-made emitters in anomaly vaults.

computronium_block.flavour: A block of matter arranged so that every atom is part of a computation. It is warm to the touch and very slightly noisy, as though it is always working. Computronium is the theoretical limit of programmable matter.
computronium_block.discovery: Once a self-improving mind made computronium possible, I compacted the ingots into blocks for building. The blocks keep thinking even when nothing is asking them to.

rift_frame_casing.flavour: A casing reinforced against tearing open: void lattice, graviton crystal and chronosteel over a hyperframe. It is built to sit at the edge of a rift between universes, and it feels faintly cold on one side.
rift_frame_casing.discovery: Stabilising a multiverse rift tore through every casing I tried. I layered a void lattice shard, which is rigid even with nothing in it, over a hyperframe with graviton crystal to hold the geometry. It held.

cosmogenic_casing.flavour: A casing built to contain the birth of a universe. Spin foam lattice, multiverse shard and cosmic neutronium are folded over a hyperlattice frame, around rift frame casing. It is unpleasantly heavy and quietly warm.
cosmogenic_casing.discovery: The Universe Forge needed a shell strong enough for a Big Bang. Spin foam is the fabric of quantum spacetime, a multiverse shard is the boundary between universes, and cosmic neutronium held them both.

stellar_frame_casing.flavour: A casing of neutronium plate over event horizon casing with a Higgs field capacitor to steady its mass. It is built to hold the weight and heat of a star, and it glows faintly gold at the seams. Standing beside it feels like standing near a hearth.
stellar_frame_casing.discovery: Stellar machines put their housings under both gravity and heat. Event horizon casing kept the energy in, neutronium plate kept the shape, and a Higgs capacitor let me adjust the mass of the casing itself.

dilithium_ore.flavour: Netherrack studded with pale violet crystals that seem to vibrate faintly, as though tuned to something. The heat of the Nether has grown them large. The name is borrowed from science fiction, and I chose it on purpose.
dilithium_ore.discovery: I spotted a violet glint in netherrack near a lava fall and broke out the first crystal. It rang when struck, like a tuning fork, and I knew it would be useful for anything that needed a steady resonance.

magnetic_confinement_casing.flavour: A casing that holds plasma away from its own walls with superconducting magnetic fields, tuned by dilithium. It works on the same principle as a tokamak. It hums, and the hum gets louder when plasma is near.
magnetic_confinement_casing.discovery: Plasma at stellar temperatures melts anything it touches. I wound superconducting coil around spacetime casing and tuned it with dilithium so the field keeps the plasma floating in the middle and away from the walls.

chronoplastic_casing.flavour: A casing laced with tachyon crystal and a chronon capacitor, so that time inside flows at a rate I can adjust. It feels slightly out of sync with the rest of the world, as though the hand touching it is one heartbeat late.
chronoplastic_casing.discovery: Time-manipulating machines bled their effects onto their own housings. I built a casing whose clock could be set independently, using tachyons to reach ahead and a chronon capacitor to store the difference.

wormhole_frame_casing.flavour: A casing threaded with negative mass and exotic matter, the ingredients a traversable wormhole needs to keep its throat open. It feels as if it is pushing my hand away and pulling it in at the same time.
wormhole_frame_casing.discovery: An Einstein-Rosen bridge collapses unless its throat is held open by negative energy. I built the frame from negative mass ingots and exotic matter crystal over a hyperframe, and the bridge stopped pinching shut.

reality_lattice_casing.flavour: A casing that contains computronium and a Bekenstein crystal to keep track of every bit of information inside it. The Bekenstein bound limits how much information a region can hold; this casing sits right at it.
reality_lattice_casing.discovery: Machines that rewrite reality need a shell that keeps the books. I combined computronium with a Bekenstein crystal over cosmogenic casing, so the casing knows exactly how much information is in it at all times.

transfinite_casing.flavour: A casing built to hold infinities: a transfinite weave over reality lattice casing, with a Russell set and a Banach-Tarski sphere worked into the seams. It looks smaller from the inside than the outside, and larger from the side.
transfinite_casing.discovery: The Axiomatic Breach Engine leaked infinities into everything near it. I used a Banach-Tarski sphere, which can be doubled, and a Russell set, which contains itself awkwardly, as a frame that would accept anything.

omnilex_casing.flavour: The casing of the final machine: crystallised law and arbor heartwood bound over a transfinite casing with a transfinite weave. It looks like wood and glass and law at the same time. It feels like nothing at all.
omnilex_casing.discovery: The Omnilex Engine simulates the Tree and the Ocean, so its casing needed both. Arbor heartwood brought the Tree, crystallised law brought the rules, and the transfinite casing held them together.

arbor_heartwood.flavour: The innermost wood of the Arbor, dense and pale, with rings that record not years but the branching of possibilities. Run a finger along the grain and it follows a different branch each time. It smells faintly of rain.
arbor_heartwood.discovery: The Arbor's core wood is different from its outer planks; the rings branch rather than circle. I cut a block from near the trunk and found each ring recorded a choice the universe had made.

bubble_universe.flavour: A sphere of an entirely separate universe, nucleated out of the inflating vacuum and sealed off from ours. Inside it, the constants are slightly different. It floats in place and is faintly warm, like a tiny sun behind fog.
bubble_universe.discovery: Eternal inflation predicts bubbles of other universes forming endlessly. I caught one at the moment it nucleated and found it would sit still in our world without expanding into it.

fractured_reality.flavour: A block of space that has cracked. Through the fractures I see pieces of other places and other times, never the same twice. It is cold, sharp-edged and quietly humming, and the hum is in a key that does not exist.
fractured_reality.discovery: I first saw fractured reality where my experiments had pushed too hard. A wall of the lab cracked and showed me a different lab behind it. I learned to respect the warning.

precision_assembly_casing.flavour: A casing of neutronium plate around a photonic processor and a femtoscale inductor, built so that nothing inside it vibrates by more than a fraction of a proton. It is dead silent and dead still. Even the dust on it seems to settle more carefully.
precision_assembly_casing.discovery: Femtoscale assembly is ruined by the slightest tremor. I combined photonic processors for control with femtoscale inductors to cancel vibration, and the casing held parts steady enough to join.

plasma_crucible_casing.flavour: A casing of chronosteel around magnetic confinement and superconducting coils, built to hold plasma at stellar temperatures for as long as needed. The air near it shimmers, and it ticks softly as it settles.
plasma_crucible_casing.discovery: Holding plasma for long periods wears magnetic casings out. I added chronosteel so the casing ages slowly relative to the plasma inside, and paired it with superconducting coils for the field.

chronosteel_coil_block.flavour: A superconducting coil wrapped in chronosteel, so that current inside it runs on its own clock. The field it makes is steadier than any ordinary coil, as though the coil had more time to think. It hums at a low, even pitch.
chronosteel_coil_block.discovery: Heavier recipes wanted hotter coils that would not drift. Wrapping a superconducting coil in chronosteel let me slow the coil's own time relative to its load, so it never quite overheats.

fractionation_casing.flavour: A casing of containment field glass and chronosteel over event horizon casing, made to separate fluids by mass and charge in a tall spire. Watching through the glass, the layers settle into neat bands.
fractionation_casing.discovery: Separating exotic fluids needed a tall, sealed column. Event horizon casing kept the fluid in, containment field glass let me watch the layers form, and chronosteel kept the separation steady.

lithography_glass.flavour: Containment field glass doped with quantum dots so that light passing through it is shaped at nanometre resolution. It projects patterns far finer than its own grain. Look closely and the glass seems to be drawing tiny circuits.
lithography_glass.discovery: Quantum lithography needed a mask that could focus light below its wavelength. Embedding quantum dots in containment field glass let them shape the light into features smaller than the light itself.

chronosteel_block.flavour: Nine chronosteel ingots fused into one block, a metal whose atoms keep slightly different time from their surroundings. It is cool, heavy and very slightly delayed, as if it reaches the hand a moment late.
chronosteel_block.discovery: Compacting chronosteel made it easier to store and gave a larger mass whose clock I could rely on. I use the blocks wherever a structure needs a steady time reference.

spacetime_alloy_block.flavour: Nine spacetime alloy ingots pressed into one block. The alloy bends spacetime around itself slightly, so the block's edges never look quite square. It is cold and surprisingly light for its size. Light glancing off it arrives a hair late.
spacetime_alloy_block.discovery: Storing the alloy as a block was the obvious step, but the block bent the space around it more noticeably than the ingots did. I keep it away from clocks.

cosmic_neutronium_block.flavour: Nine ingots of cosmic neutronium fused into a block denser than the inside of a neutron star. It is hard to pick up and harder to put down gently. It casts a faint, cold shadow even in full light. A few faint points of light swim deep inside it.
cosmic_neutronium_block.discovery: Cosmic neutronium was too precious to leave loose. Pressing it into a block was easy; moving the block afterwards was not, but the supply is safe.

dilithium_block.flavour: Dilithium crystals fused into one solid block that rings when struck and glows a soft violet. The resonance carries through the floor, and anything metal nearby picks up a faint hum. In a quiet room the note is just audible, steady and clean, and it never seems to fade.
dilithium_block.discovery: Compacting dilithium crystals for storage turned their individual tones into a single, pure note. I keep the block near tuning-sensitive machines and they seem to like it.

void_lattice_block.flavour: Void lattice shards compacted into a block - a crystal of empty sites that is rigid even though there is nothing in it. Looking at it feels like looking at a hole in the world with very clean edges. It weighs almost nothing.
void_lattice_block.discovery: Pressing void lattice shards together made a block that still had nothing in it but held its shape anyway. It is the strangest building material I have, and it stacks neatly.

neutronium_plating.flavour: Neutronium rolled into flat plates and riveted onto a block face. It is grey, dense and almost reflective, with seams that look as though they were drawn with a ruler. It gives a lab the look of a reactor vault.
neutronium_plating.discovery: I had more neutronium than I needed for machines, so I started plating walls with it. It is overbuilt for decoration, but it never dents.

neutronium_tiles.flavour: Neutronium cut into small square tiles and laid in a grid. The tiles are perfectly flat and very slightly cold, and footsteps on them sound muffled, as if the floor is absorbing more than sound. Each joint is so fine a hair would not fit in it.
neutronium_tiles.discovery: Tiling neutronium was a way to use offcuts from plating. The grid pattern makes the floors of a lab easy to read at a glance.

neutronium_bricks.flavour: Neutronium shaped into bricks and stacked with careful offset joints. It looks like an ordinary brick wall made of something no ordinary wall should be made of. It does not echo. The bricks never chip or weather, and running a hand along them is like stroking cold iron.
neutronium_bricks.discovery: I wanted walls that looked built rather than plated, so I cut neutronium into bricks. The mortar is the strong force, more or less.

neutronium_pillar.flavour: A column of neutronium with fluted sides, built to carry loads that would buckle any ordinary pillar. It is heavy enough to feel rooted and smooth enough to feel cold. Flat-topped and square-shouldered, it looks like it was designed to outlast the building around it.
neutronium_pillar.discovery: Pillars were a practical need in larger labs. Neutronium columns carried everything I put on them, so I stopped worrying about the ceiling.

polished_cherenkov_quartz.flavour: Cherenkov quartz polished until its surface is glassy and its glow is even across the whole face. In a dark room it gives off a cool blue light like water around a reactor core. My reflection in it is tinted blue and very slightly brighter than I am.
polished_cherenkov_quartz.discovery: Raw Cherenkov quartz glows unevenly. Polishing the block smoothed the light, and I began using it for walls where I wanted a gentle, cool shine.

cherenkov_bricks.flavour: Cherenkov quartz cut into small bricks, each one glowing softly blue along its edges. A wall of them looks like a shallow pool at night. They are smooth and slightly cool to the touch. Every joint carries its own thin line of blue light, so the whole wall seems sketched in glow.
cherenkov_bricks.discovery: I cut Cherenkov quartz into bricks to make glowing walls with more texture than plain blocks. The light catches along every seam.

cherenkov_pillar.flavour: A column of Cherenkov quartz that glows along its length with an even blue. Placed at a doorway it reads like a beam of light holding up the lintel. It is cool and faintly humming. Rows of them along a corridor make it feel like walking beneath a reactor pool.
cherenkov_pillar.discovery: Pillars of Cherenkov quartz gave the labs a sense of structure and a little light. They were easy to cut and look better than they have any right to.

cherenkov_lamp.flavour: A lamp of Cherenkov quartz with glowstone at its heart, so the blue Cherenkov glow is amplified into a strong, clean light. It is the colour of a reactor pool, and as calming. It never flickers and never warms, and the blue makes every surface it touches look freshly cleaned.
cherenkov_lamp.discovery: Cherenkov quartz alone glowed too faintly to light a room. Adding glowstone dust to a block of it pushed the glow into a proper lamp.

chronosteel_plating.flavour: Chronosteel rolled into plates and fixed to a block face. Its sheen is cool and slightly blurred, as if the surface had moved a moment before it was seen. It gives a wall a clean, mechanical look. Rivets mark each corner, set in perfectly even rows.
chronosteel_plating.discovery: I had spare chronosteel, so I plated walls with it. The blurred reflections are a side effect of the metal's own clock and I have grown fond of them.

chronosteel_hazard_panel.flavour: A chronosteel panel painted with warning stripes, used to mark doorways, machine edges and anything I do not want to walk into. The stripes look very slightly out of step with each other. Yellow and black on dull metal - a language every lab in every universe seems to share.
chronosteel_hazard_panel.discovery: After walking into a running time field once, I started marking hazards. Chronosteel panels with stripes were the clearest way to say keep out.

chronosteel_vent.flavour: A chronosteel grille that lets air pass between rooms. The slats are angled to keep light out and air moving, and a faint draught always seems to be flowing through it, even when the room is still. The slats never collect dust, though I have never cleaned them.
chronosteel_vent.discovery: Labs full of machines get stuffy. Chronosteel vents were the obvious fix, and they look the part. The slats were angled by trial and error until the hum of the machines dropped.

chronosteel_pillar.flavour: A column of chronosteel, banded and fluted, that carries a load without complaint. It reflects light in a slightly delayed blur and gives a doorway the feel of an engine room. Its bands are spaced at regular intervals, like the ticks on a clock face.
chronosteel_pillar.discovery: Chronosteel pillars were stronger than I needed and looked better than stone. I used them to frame machine halls. They also make a reliable time reference.

spacetime_panel.flavour: A panel of spacetime alloy whose surface seems to bend inward slightly, as if the wall behind it were further away than it is. It is cool, smooth and very faintly disorienting to look at for long. Its edges line up neatly in rows.
spacetime_panel.discovery: Spacetime alloy made interesting walls, but solid blocks were too much. Panels gave me the effect without the weight. They are also easy to cut to size.

spacetime_tiles.flavour: Spacetime alloy cut into tiles that never quite look square. Each tile bends the space around it a fraction, so the grid seems to ripple gently as I walk across it. Nothing placed on them ever rolls, even though the floor looks curved. The ripple is optical, not physical, which I confirmed with a marble.
spacetime_tiles.discovery: I tiled a floor with spacetime alloy to see what would happen. The floor ripples, but it holds, and I liked it enough to keep it.

spacetime_bricks.flavour: Spacetime alloy bricks stacked in an offset pattern. The wall seems slightly curved even when perfectly straight, and its shadows fall a fraction off where they should. The mortar lines bend gently, like a grid drawn on a stretched sheet, and the effect is strongest at the corners.
spacetime_bricks.discovery: I wanted a spacetime wall with texture, so I cut the alloy into bricks. The wall looks like it is leaning into another dimension, but it is not.

cosmic_tiles.flavour: Cosmic neutronium cut into dark tiles that seem to have tiny points of light deep inside them, like stars seen through a deep well. The floor they make feels impossibly solid. The tiny lights drift very slowly if I watch them long enough, like stars wheeling over a night.
cosmic_tiles.discovery: I had offcuts of cosmic neutronium and laid them as tiles. The faint lights inside them were a surprise, and I left them as they were.

cosmic_plating.flavour: Cosmic neutronium rolled into plating, dark as space with faint pinpricks of light. A wall of it looks like a window onto the night sky that happens to be load-bearing. Running a hand over it feels like touching cold glass, and the lights inside never quite stay still.
cosmic_plating.discovery: Plating walls with cosmic neutronium was extravagant, but the effect was worth it. It is the closest thing to a sky I have indoors.

computronium_panel.flavour: A panel of computronium with fine glowing traces running across its face, like a circuit board that is thinking. It is warm and faintly busy to the touch. The traces brighten when someone stands close, then fade once they walk away, as though the panel had finished noticing them.
computronium_panel.discovery: Computronium walls were too warm as solid blocks. Thin panels gave me the look of a working computer without heating the room.

computronium_tiles.flavour: Computronium cut into tiles, each one lit by faint, shifting traces. A floor of them flickers softly, as if computing something about whoever walks across it. Patterns chase each other across the joints between tiles, too fast to follow, and settle into stillness when the room empties.
computronium_tiles.discovery: I tiled a floor with computronium offcuts. It flickers gently underfoot, and I am almost sure it is only decorative. It has never miscounted anything.

computronium_lamp.flavour: A computronium block lit from within by glowstone, its traces brightened into a steady, warm glow. It looks like a terminal screen turned into a lamp. The light pulses almost imperceptibly, a slow rhythm like breathing. Close up, the traces under the glow are still busy rearranging themselves.
computronium_lamp.discovery: Computronium's own glow was too faint to read by. Adding glowstone dust turned a block into a proper lamp that still hums with computation.

polished_dilithium.flavour: Dilithium polished to a mirror finish, its violet colour deep and even. It rings very faintly when touched, and a room of it seems to hum one long note. The surface is clear enough to see my own reflection tinted violet, and fingerprints vanish from it almost as soon as they appear.
polished_dilithium.discovery: Raw dilithium blocks were rough and uneven. Polishing them brought out the colour, and I started using them for walls I wanted to look calm.

dilithium_lamp.flavour: A dilithium block with glowstone at its centre, so the violet crystal shines with a soft, even light. It hums a single note when lit. The light is steady and gentle, more like dusk than daylight, and the note it hums sits comfortably beneath conversation. It is the lamp I leave on at night.
dilithium_lamp.discovery: Dilithium glowed only faintly on its own. Adding glowstone dust gave me a violet lamp that also hums, which I find oddly soothing.

void_bricks.flavour: Void lattice cut into bricks - rigid blocks of nothing stacked with careful joints. The wall looks like a pattern of very clean holes in the world. Each brick has crisp, flawless edges, and the joints between them are the only part that looks like ordinary matter. Torchlight seems to fall into them.
void_bricks.discovery: I wanted a wall that looked like empty space with structure. Void lattice bricks were exactly that, and they stack as well as stone.

void_tiles.flavour: Void lattice cut into flat tiles. A floor of them looks like standing on a grid laid over nothing at all, and it is perfectly solid underfoot. My footsteps make no echo at all, and a dropped tool lands silently, as though the floor were listening too hard to make any sound.
void_tiles.discovery: I tiled a floor with void lattice to see if it would hold. It held, and looking down at it is an experience I recommend once.

void_pillar.flavour: A column of void lattice, rigid emptiness standing upright. It carries weight without any matter inside it, which still seems wrong every time I look at it. Torchlight passes straight into it and does not come out, so the column reads as a perfectly black stripe standing in the room.
void_pillar.discovery: I needed pillars in a void-lattice room and cut them from the same material. They hold up the ceiling with nothing at all.

stellar_lamp.flavour: A stellar frame casing with glowstone at its heart, so it shines with a warm, golden light like a small star seen through a window. It is warm to stand next to. The colour is the warm yellow of a midday sun, steady and comforting, and the seams of the casing glow brightest of all.
stellar_lamp.discovery: Stellar frame casing glowed at its seams already. Adding glowstone dust turned it into a lamp that gives off starlight. It is my favourite light.

cloaking_glass.flavour: A pane of metamaterial that bends light around itself, so the glass is nearly invisible from any angle. Only the edges betray it, as a faint distortion in the room. Walking past it, the room behind seems to shift a little too smoothly, like a painted backdrop.
cloaking_glass.discovery: Metamaterials can steer light around an object. I built them into glass to see if I could make a window that vanished, and it nearly did.

hex_glass.flavour: Glass held together by a hexagonal force field, like a honeycomb of light. Each cell glows faintly at its edges. It is strong and very slightly warm to the touch. Tapping it makes each hexagon ring separately, a soft chiming that dies away quickly.
hex_glass.discovery: I wanted a stronger glass for labs. A hexagonal field pattern spread stress evenly across every cell, and the honeycomb glow came free.

arbor_planks.flavour: Planks cut from the Arbor, pale and fine-grained, with faint branching lines running along their length. The wood smells of rain and seems to grow warmer when people walk across it. Nails go in easily and never split it.
arbor_planks.discovery: I split Arbor heartwood into planks for building. The grain branched instead of running straight, and every board I cut was slightly different.

spacetime_alloy_coil_block.flavour: A coil of spacetime alloy wound over a chronosteel coil, cooled by a cryocooler and soldered with exotic solder. It runs hotter and holds heavier recipes than any coil before it, and the air around it shimmers.
spacetime_alloy_coil_block.discovery: Component tiers taught me that a structure is only as strong as its weakest coil. I wound spacetime alloy over chronosteel with a topological processor to manage it, and the coil carried loads the old one could not.

cosmic_neutronium_coil_block.flavour: A coil of cosmic neutronium over spacetime alloy, cooled cryogenically and threaded with pentaquark shards. It runs hotter than anything below it and seems to pull faintly on the room. The windings are so dense that they barely look like separate turns.
cosmic_neutronium_coil_block.discovery: The Transcendent Plasma Forge demanded hotter coils still. I wound cosmic neutronium over a spacetime alloy coil, with a hyperdimensional processor to handle the load and pentaquark shards to stabilise it.

transfinite_coil_block.flavour: A coil of hypernova alloy wound around an aleph-null shard over a cosmic neutronium coil, superconducting at room temperature. It carries a current that never quite finishes counting itself. The windings seem to continue past the point where the coil should end.
transfinite_coil_block.discovery: Above stellar-core temperatures even cosmic neutronium coils fail. I wound hypernova alloy around an aleph-null shard with a room-temperature superconductor and a cosmic processor, and the coil held.

graviton_field_emitter.flavour: A field emitter upgraded with a graviton crystal and a gravitic lens element, so it projects gravity as well as fields. It weighs more on one side than the other, and that side changes. Dust drifts toward its face and settles in slow rings.
graviton_field_emitter.discovery: Better emitters let a multiblock run more parallels. I added a graviton crystal and a gravitic lens to a field emitter, with a hyperdimensional processor and hyperon crystal to shape the field. It projected gravity cleanly.

axiomatic_field_emitter.flavour: A field emitter that projects not forces but rules - a small region where a chosen axiom holds or does not. It is built on a graviton emitter with an axiom fragment, and it feels like holding a principle.
axiomatic_field_emitter.discovery: Axiom theory showed that axioms can be distilled and edited. I mounted an axiom fragment on a graviton field emitter with transcendent metal, a horizon shard and a transfinite processor, and the emitter began projecting law instead of force.

vacuum_beam_pipe.flavour: A pipe of containment field glass and metamaterial lined with Casimir plates, so the space inside is emptier than empty. A particle beam runs through it without touching anything at all. Peering inside shows nothing, not even a reflection.
vacuum_beam_pipe.discovery: Particle beams scatter off any gas. I lined containment glass with Casimir plates, which push out even virtual particles, and wrapped it in metamaterial. The beam stopped scattering.

dipole_bending_magnet.flavour: A superconducting dipole magnet on a neutronium frame that bends a charged particle beam into a circle. Its field is perfectly uniform across the gap. Metal tools drift toward it. Its field lines would draw a perfect rectangle in iron filings.
dipole_bending_magnet.discovery: A synchrotron needs magnets to curve the beam back on itself. I wound a dipole around a superconducting coil block on a neutronium plate and the beam turned exactly as calculated.

quadrupole_focusing_magnet.flavour: A quadrupole magnet with four pole tips that squeeze a particle beam in one direction while stretching it in the other. Pairs of them focus a beam the way lenses focus light. Its four poles alternate north and south around the bore, and the field between them is zero at the very centre.
quadrupole_focusing_magnet.discovery: A beam spreads as it travels. Quadrupoles focus it like lenses. I fitted quadrupole pole tips to a superconducting coil on spacetime casing and the beam stayed tight.

rf_accelerating_cavity.flavour: A resonant cavity driven by a tachyon klystron that gives each passing particle a precisely timed kick. Inside, radio waves bounce in a standing pattern. It hums at a frequency I can feel in my teeth.
rf_accelerating_cavity.discovery: Particles in a ring need repeated kicks to gain energy. I built an RF resonator cell into spacetime casing and drove it with a tachyon klystron, so every kick arrived on time.

cryogenic_cooling_jacket.flavour: A jacket of containment field glass around a cryocooler, built to keep superconducting parts close to absolute zero. Frost forms on its outer face within seconds. Breath fogs in front of it, and the metal near it creaks quietly as it contracts in the cold.
cryogenic_cooling_jacket.discovery: Superconductors fail if they warm up. I wrapped a cryocooler unit in containment glass over spacetime casing and the parts inside stayed cold indefinitely.

turbomolecular_vacuum_pump.flavour: A pump whose rotor spins so fast that its blades knock gas molecules out of the chamber one by one. It whines at a pitch just below hearing. Ultra-high vacuum starts here. The rotor blades are angled like a jet turbine, and they spin faster than the eye can follow.
turbomolecular_vacuum_pump.discovery: Mechanical pumps stop at a rough vacuum. A turbomolecular rotor, driven by a superconducting coil on neutronium and spacetime casing, kicked out the remaining molecules.

calorimeter_detector_array.flavour: An array of scintillator crystals and pixel trackers that records where a particle went and how much energy it carried. A quantum processor reads the flashes. The crystals glow faintly when hit. Tiny flashes ripple across it.
calorimeter_detector_array.discovery: To know what a collision produced I needed to measure both position and energy. I combined scintillators for energy, pixel trackers for paths and a quantum processor to read them.

plasma_injection_nozzle.flavour: A nozzle that fires plasma into a confinement chamber at a precisely controlled rate. Magnetic confinement steers it, a cryocooler keeps the coils cold, and the tip glows white when in use. The air around the tip crackles.
plasma_injection_nozzle.discovery: Feeding plasma into a nucleosynthesis chamber needs precision. I fitted a plasma nozzle tip into magnetic confinement casing with a superconducting coil block and a cryocooler, and the plasma went exactly where I aimed.

graviton_lens_array.flavour: An array of gravitic lens elements that bend spacetime to focus gravitational waves, the way a glass lens bends light. Inside, the space seems to pinch toward the centre. Straight edges seen through its centre appear to bow outward, as if viewed through a thick drop of water.
graviton_lens_array.discovery: Gravitational lensing is real: massive objects bend light. I set gravitic lens elements into event horizon casing over a hyperframe, and the array focused gravitational waves to a point.

hawking_radiation_collector.flavour: A collector of Hawking absorber plates and entangled photons that catches the faint radiation evaporating black holes give off. It is warm, and the warmth comes from somewhere it should not. It glitters faintly with stray photons.
hawking_radiation_collector.discovery: Black holes radiate, very faintly, as Hawking predicted. I combined absorber plates with entangled photons to catch the partners of the emitted particles and mounted them on a field emitter.

quantum_error_correction_core.flavour: A core that protects a quantum computer's fragile states by spreading each logical qubit across many physical ones and fixing errors as they happen. It hums with a steady, careful rhythm. Its lights blink in careful patterns.
quantum_error_correction_core.discovery: Qubits decohere constantly. Error correction encodes one logical qubit in many, so errors can be detected and undone. I combined a quantum processor with an error-correction lattice on spacetime casing.

spacetime_anchor_pylon.flavour: A pylon that pins a patch of spacetime in place, built around a spacetime anchor core and a chronosteel coil. The ground around it feels unusually solid, as if gravity had made its mind up. Compasses near it point steady.
spacetime_anchor_pylon.discovery: Large machines warped the ground they stood on. I built a pylon around an anchor core with a chronosteel coil and hyperframe casing, and the warping stopped at its edge.

dimensional_stabiliser.flavour: A stabiliser that holds the number of dimensions in a region fixed while machines nearby try to change it. A dimensional stabiliser matrix sets the count, and a field emitter enforces it. Near it, corners look properly square.
dimensional_stabiliser.discovery: Hyperdimensional machines kept bleeding extra dimensions into the lab. I built a stabiliser around a dimensional stabiliser matrix with a field emitter and hyperframe casing, and the room stayed three-dimensional.

causal_shielding_plate.flavour: A plate of chronosteel and causal shield lattice that keeps cause and effect in the right order on either side. It feels slightly ahead of the moment, as though it knew I was going to touch it. Its surface is faintly lined.
causal_shielding_plate.discovery: Time machines can leak effects before their causes. I layered a causal shield lattice on chronosteel and chronoplastic casing, and the plate kept the order straight.

stellar_containment_plate.flavour: A plate of degenerate armour and spacetime alloy over magnetic confinement casing, built to hold back the pressure and heat of a star. It is impossibly heavy and faintly warm. Heat haze clings to its face even when the machine it guards is cold and silent.
stellar_containment_plate.discovery: Stellar machines needed walls that would not buckle. I combined degenerate armour plate with spacetime alloy and magnetic confinement, and the plate held a star's pressure.

axiom_stone.flavour: Pale, smooth stone that seems to be made of definitions. Each block holds its shape because it has been told to. It is cool and faintly humming, like a theorem being proved. Its surface is unmarked except for faint, regular lines, like ruled paper for a proof yet to be written.
axiom_stone.discovery: In the realm of axioms, everything rests on this stone. I mined a piece to see what it was and found it underlay both the natural numbers and the axiom schemas I had been studying.

golden_ratio_glass.flavour: Glass made with a transcendental crystal so that its proportions follow the golden ratio at every scale. Each pane is divided into smaller panes in the same ratio, forever. It looks calm and endlessly deep.
golden_ratio_glass.discovery: I first found it in Euclid's Vault and in the wake of a Fractal Wyrm. Later I made my own by fusing a transcendental crystal into containment field glass, and the ratio appeared on its own.

prime_number_ore.flavour: Axiom stone threaded with veins that appear only at prime positions - never at a composite one, and never in a pattern I can predict. It feels slightly irregular, like counting with a missing beat. The ore is rarer deeper down.
prime_number_ore.discovery: I mined along a seam in axiom stone and found the veins only at prime intervals. The ore held numbers that could not be divided, and I kept every piece.

transcendental_ore.flavour: Axiom stone shot through with crystals of transcendental numbers - pi, e and their kin, which are not roots of any polynomial. The veins never repeat and never end. It is cool and faintly bright. Its sparkle never repeats.
transcendental_ore.discovery: Deep in the axiom stone I found crystals whose patterns never repeated. Testing them, I found they were transcendental. I keep a sample in my notebook as a reminder.
